## First public preview

Rei is an Electron desktop workspace for bingo. This preview bundles a platform-matching **bingo v0.6.4** runtime; existing bingo configuration remains owned by bingo.

### Included

- Conversations without a required project: start in a private temporary workspace, or attach a folder.
- Streaming responses, compact semantic tool activity, interactive approvals, conversation history and independent text drafts.
- A compact Environment panel for subagents and rooms, with live journal activity and explicit conversation routing.
- Read-only tracked Git review, runtime-discovered skills and automation request composition.
- Safe journal images, Mermaid diagrams and KaTeX math; external images load only after a click.
- Searchable model selection, reasoning-effort controls and English/Simplified Chinese UI.
- A right-side isolated browser, agent-generated ShowPage pages, and independent terminal tabs that close when their shells exit.
- Provider setup, system/light/dark appearance, a centered empty composer and stable thread ordering.
- A required platform-matching bundled runtime; selecting an external executable is optional.

### Before installing

- **Preview quality; manual updates.** This is not a signed or notarized stable release. macOS and Windows may show publisher/security warnings. Verify downloads using `SHA256SUMS.txt`; do not disable system security globally.
- You still need to configure a model provider. Cloud OAuth/accounts were not exercised using real credentials in automated tests.
- **Windows is not at full agent-tool parity:** the GUI and embedded native terminal target Windows, but bingo's agent `Bash` tool is currently Unix-only. Do not rely on general agent shell-execution workflows on Windows.
- Agent and room views are journal-backed; this preview does not include a full file explorer. File/source previews show recorded content, not arbitrary current files on disk.
- Temporary-workspace files are not a permanent project location. Attach a project folder for work you want to keep there.
- The terminal runs your local shell with your user privileges. Browser pages are isolated from the application bridge and Node.js; normal web links open in-app, while sign-in has an explicit system-browser path.

Installer assets are published only after their corresponding build and automated checks succeed. Native CI checks do not replace hands-on device testing or an independent security audit.
